project.name: icarKno
project.description: icarKno is an AI-powered document intelligence platform that enables intelligent querying, summarization, and knowledge extraction from documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, CSV, XLSX) via a Flask/FastAPI backend with hybrid vector and keyword search, multi-language support, and WhatsApp/REST integrations.

nodes.name: result_synthesis_service.py
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a final structured answer from multiple search results by formatting them with citations and prompting an LLM to produce a JSON response, with robust parsing/repair logic, retries, and both streaming and non-streaming synthesis paths.

nodes.name: SynthesisResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing the final synthesized answer, including reasoning steps, confidence level, follow-up questions, synthesis metadata, and answer completeness.

nodes.name: ResultSynthesisService
nodes.summary: Builds citation-annotated synthesis prompts from SearchResult objects, invokes an LLM (with retry logic) to produce a JSON-structured answer, repairs malformed JSON responses, and supports a streaming variant that yields tokens as they arrive.

nodes.name: get_result_synthesis_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a ResultSynthesisService instance.

nodes.name: search_execution_service.py
nodes.summary: Executes a planned SearchStrategy by building a dependency-ordered execution plan, running document/SQL/summary/hybrid searches per instruction through the context provider, deduplicating, and ranking the combined results.

nodes.name: SearchResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing the outcome of one search instruction's execution: instruction index, success flag, content, metadata, and error message.

nodes.name: ExecutionPlan
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing the ordered phases of search instructions to execute, along with total instruction count and estimated duration.

nodes.name: SearchExecutionService
nodes.summary: Builds a dependency-aware execution plan from search instructions, dispatches each instruction to the appropriate document/SQL/summary/hybrid search method via the context provider service, and deduplicates and ranks the aggregated results.

nodes.name: get_search_execution_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a SearchExecutionService instance.

nodes.name: ask.py
nodes.summary: Provides a lightweight demo question-answering path that checks for a cached previous question, queries the SQL database for relevant data, and asks the standard LLM to produce a response.

nodes.name: checkPreviousQn
nodes.summary: Reads a session's previously stored question from disk, if present, to support continuation-aware demo responses.

nodes.name: get_demo_response
nodes.summary: Generates a demo answer for a user query by querying the database, incorporating the previous question for context, and invoking the standard LLM to compose the final response.

nodes.name: doc_summary.py
nodes.summary: Implements document summarization for a session's uploaded files: extractive summarization via BERT (Summarizer) to select important sentences, dynamic sentence-count tuning, and LLM-based abstractive summarization across selected or all available folders.

nodes.name: DocumentSummaryService
nodes.summary: Manages per-file extractive (BERT-based) summarization plus metadata caching, and provides LLM-driven abstractive summarization that combines important sentences from specified or all available document folders for a session.

nodes.name: get_summary_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a DocumentSummaryService instance.

nodes.name: create_abstractive_summary
nodes.summary: Module-level convenience wrapper delegating to the shared DocumentSummaryService's create_abstractive_summary method.

nodes.name: summarize_document
nodes.summary: Module-level convenience wrapper delegating to the shared DocumentSummaryService's summarize_document method, used by other services as the summary context entry point.

nodes.name: sql_db.py
nodes.summary: Manages per-session SQLite database creation from uploaded CSV/Excel files, sanitizes identifiers, generates SQL queries from natural language via an LLM SQL chain, executes them safely, and stores generated table summaries.

nodes.name: sanitize_identifier
nodes.summary: Sanitizes a string into a safe SQL identifier (table/column name) by stripping disallowed characters and truncating to a maximum length.

nodes.name: get_db_engine
nodes.summary: Creates or connects to a per-session SQLite database engine, verifying connectivity and falling back to engine creation if the database doesn't yet exist.

nodes.name: process_file
nodes.summary: Parses an uploaded CSV or Excel file into pandas DataFrame(s) and writes each sheet/table into the session's SQL database under a sanitized table name.

nodes.name: create_database_with_tables
nodes.summary: Creates a new session database and ingests a batch of uploaded files into it, persisting table metadata to a JSON file for later lookup.

nodes.name: add_tables_to_existing_db
nodes.summary: Adds new tables from additional uploaded files to an already-existing session database, updating the persisted table metadata.

nodes.name: execute_safe_query
nodes.summary: Executes a SQL query against the engine with parameter binding, attempting an automatic LIMIT/quoting repair pass if the first execution fails.

nodes.name: clean_sql_query
nodes.summary: Strips LLM-generated SQL output of markdown fences and other formatting noise to extract a clean, executable SQL statement.

nodes.name: generate_sql_query
nodes.summary: Uses a LangChain SQL query chain backed by the standard LLM to translate a natural-language question into a SQL query against the session database, then cleans the raw output.

nodes.name: query_database
nodes.summary: End-to-end helper that resolves the session's DB engine, generates a SQL query from a natural-language question, executes it safely, and returns the results.

nodes.name: store_table_info
nodes.summary: Generates and persists descriptive summaries for each table in a session's database (sampling rows via SQL queries), writing the combined summary text and metadata to disk for later use as data context.

nodes.name: adaptive_search_service.py
nodes.summary: Runs an iterative, multi-round search loop that progressively refines queries using LLM-based evaluation until results are deemed sufficient or limits are reached, deduplicating and combining content across rounds.

nodes.name: AdaptiveSearchResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing the outcome of an adaptive search run, including success flag, iteration count, final content, all intermediate results, and evaluation history.

nodes.name: AdaptiveSearchService
nodes.summary: Coordinates iterative search execution: enhances queries with chat context, executes searches against document/data/summary resources, evaluates sufficiency via the evaluation service, and deduplicates combined results across rounds.

nodes.name: get_adaptive_search_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns an AdaptiveSearchService instance.

nodes.name: context_provider_service.py
nodes.summary: Centralizes retrieval of document, SQL data, and summary context for a user session, enriching search queries with conversational context (references, clarifications, continuations) before querying Elasticsearch, the SQL database, or the summarizer.

nodes.name: ContextProviderService
nodes.summary: Provides document, SQL, and summary context retrieval for a chat session, augmenting search queries with conversational history and merging full table chunks into Elasticsearch retrieval results.

nodes.name: get_context_provider_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a ContextProviderService instance.

nodes.name: creative_reasoning_service.py
nodes.summary: Handles open-ended, creative-style query processing by running adaptive search, synthesizing results into a structured answer via LLM, and generating follow-up questions, with both streaming and non-streaming entry points.

nodes.name: CreativeReasoningService
nodes.summary: Orchestrates creative-mode query answering: runs adaptive search, synthesizes a JSON-structured response with an LLM, parses/repairs the response, generates follow-up questions, and provides fallback/error responses on failure.

nodes.name: get_creative_reasoning_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a CreativeReasoningService instance.

nodes.name: llm_service.py
nodes.summary: Defines a custom LangChain-compatible chat model that talks to a self-hosted GPU inference server over HTTP, plus factory functions exposing pre-configured LLM instances tuned for different use cases (fast, standard, comprehensive, creative, code, streaming).
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the LangChain BaseChatModel interface (_generate/_stream) to wrap a custom GPU server API, including SSE-style streaming token parsing.

nodes.name: GPUServerChatModel
nodes.summary: Custom LangChain BaseChatModel implementation that sends chat messages to a self-hosted GPU inference server via REST and supports both synchronous generation and token streaming.

nodes.name: LLMType
nodes.summary: Enum identifying the available LLM configuration profiles (fast, standard, comprehensive, creative, code) used to select model behavior.

nodes.name: _make_llm
nodes.summary: Internal helper that instantiates a GPUServerChatModel with the given keyword overrides.

nodes.name: get_fast_llm
nodes.summary: Returns an LLM instance configured for fast, low-latency responses.

nodes.name: get_standard_llm
nodes.summary: Returns an LLM instance configured with standard, balanced settings used across general query answering.

nodes.name: get_comprehensive_llm
nodes.summary: Returns an LLM instance configured for comprehensive, higher-token-budget reasoning tasks such as strategy planning and synthesis.

nodes.name: get_creative_llm
nodes.summary: Returns an LLM instance tuned with higher temperature for creative-mode response generation.

nodes.name: get_code_llm
nodes.summary: Returns an LLM instance configured for code-related generation tasks.

nodes.name: get_streaming_llm
nodes.summary: Builds an LLM configured for streaming output, attaching the provided callback handlers and binding the requested LLM type's configuration.

nodes.name: reasoning_strategy_service.py
nodes.summary: Analyzes a user's query with an LLM to produce a structured multi-step search strategy (decomposed sub-queries, types, priorities, dependencies), converting it into executable search instructions with a rule-based fallback when LLM parsing fails.

nodes.name: SearchType
nodes.summary: Enum of supported search categories such as document, SQL/data, summary, and hybrid search.

nodes.name: SearchPriority
nodes.summary: Enum of execution priority levels used to order and parallelize search instructions.

nodes.name: SearchInstruction
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing one executable search step, including its query, type, priority, instructions, expected information, and dependencies on other steps.

nodes.name: SearchStrategy
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing the LLM-produced overall search plan: reasoning, query breakdown, list of searches, synthesis approach, and confidence level.

nodes.name: ReasoningStrategyService
nodes.summary: Uses a comprehensive LLM with a Pydantic output parser to analyze a query and available resources, generating a SearchStrategy; converts that strategy into SearchInstruction objects and falls back to a rule-based strategy on failure.

nodes.name: get_reasoning_strategy_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a ReasoningStrategyService instance.

nodes.name: result_evaluation_service.py
nodes.summary: Evaluates whether accumulated search results sufficiently answer a query using an LLM-based judgment (with keyword-overlap fallback) and generates focused follow-up queries to fill identified gaps.

nodes.name: EvaluationResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the outcome of a sufficiency evaluation: whether results are sufficient, a confidence score, missing aspects, reasoning, and suggested refinements.

nodes.name: ResultEvaluationService
nodes.summary: Judges whether search results sufficiently answer a query via an LLM call (with a heuristic keyword-overlap fallback) and proposes refined/focused follow-up search queries when results are insufficient.

nodes.name: get_result_evaluation_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton-style accessor that constructs and returns a ResultEvaluationService instance.

nodes.name: auth_service.py
nodes.summary: Provides a lightweight authentication service used across API blueprints to validate requests, derive session names, and issue tokens.

nodes.name: AuthService
nodes.summary: Encapsulates authentication logic including request authentication, full session name resolution, and token creation, used by nearly every authenticated API route.

nodes.name: get_auth_service
nodes.summary: Factory/accessor function that lazily constructs and returns a shared AuthService instance, optionally bound to the Flask app.

nodes.name: chat_history_manager.py
nodes.summary: Central service for persisting and retrieving chat history in MongoDB, handling session/chat naming, context retrieval strategies (recent, reference, adaptive, LLM-based), note-taking, session limits, cleanup, and deletion.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines deterministic recent-message context retrieval with an LLM-based context-need analysis strategy, blending heuristic and model-driven decisions.

nodes.name: ChatHistoryManager
nodes.summary: Large service class managing the full lifecycle of chat sessions and messages in MongoDB: storage, naming, context window strategies, notes, statistics, cleanup, and deletion.

nodes.name: get_chat_history_manager
nodes.summary: Factory/accessor function that lazily constructs and returns a shared ChatHistoryManager instance.

nodes.name: stt_service.py
nodes.summary: Speech-to-text service that connects to an external Vexyl STT backend over HTTP/WebSocket, transcribing audio bytes or streaming PCM audio chunks with language code translation.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges async WebSocket streaming transcription into a synchronous queue-based interface using an asyncio event loop run in a background thread.

nodes.name: _async_stream_stt
nodes.summary: Async helper that streams PCM audio chunks to the Vexyl STT WebSocket endpoint and pushes transcription results onto a queue for synchronous consumption.

nodes.name: get_stt_service
nodes.summary: Factory/accessor function that lazily constructs and returns a shared STTService instance.

nodes.name: STTService
nodes.summary: Encapsulates speech-to-text operations including batch transcription of audio bytes, streaming transcription, and connectivity testing against the Vexyl backend.

nodes.name: tts_service.py
nodes.summary: Text-to-speech service that connects to an external Vexyl TTS backend, cleaning input text and streaming synthesized audio back via async-to-sync bridging.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a dedicated background thread running an asyncio event loop to bridge async audio-streaming generators into a synchronous queue consumed by Flask response generators.

nodes.name: _clean_text_for_tts
nodes.summary: Sanitizes and normalizes input text (stripping markdown/special characters) before sending it to the TTS engine for synthesis.

nodes.name: _async_generate_audio_stream
nodes.summary: Async generator that streams synthesized audio chunks from the Vexyl TTS WebSocket backend for a given text and language code.

nodes.name: _run_async_generator_to_queue
nodes.summary: Drives an async generator to completion on an event loop, pushing each yielded item onto a thread-safe queue for synchronous consumers.

nodes.name: get_tts_service
nodes.summary: Factory/accessor function that lazily constructs and returns a shared TTSService instance.

nodes.name: TTSService
nodes.summary: Encapsulates text-to-speech operations including streaming audio generation, buffered audio generation, and connectivity testing against the Vexyl backend.

nodes.name: auth.py
nodes.summary: Flask blueprint defining authentication-related API routes; currently exposes only a simple health check endpoint while real auth logic lives in auth_service.

nodes.name: healthcheck
nodes.summary: Health check route handler that returns a JSON status message confirming the app is running.

nodes.name: documents.py
nodes.summary: Flask blueprint exposing document and container management routes: free-trial uploads, authenticated file/URL uploads, file retrieval, container renaming, listing, and deletion.

nodes.name: free_trial
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated trial endpoint that accepts files and URLs, validates them, and forwards processing to the document service.

nodes.name: upload
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that creates a new container/session and uploads files and URLs into it via the document service.

nodes.name: add_upload
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that adds additional files/URLs to an existing document container/session.

nodes.name: fetch_file
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that resolves a stored file's path via the document service and streams it back to the client.

nodes.name: update_timestamp
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that updates the last-activity timestamp of a document container/session.

nodes.name: rename_container_route
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that renames a document container via the document service.

nodes.name: get_containers
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that lists all document containers/sessions belonging to a user.

nodes.name: delete_container_route
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that deletes a document container/session via the document service.

nodes.name: queries.py
nodes.summary: Large Flask blueprint that powers the query/chat experience: image captioning, trial and authenticated Q&A (sync and streaming), text-to-speech responses, speech-to-text transcription, chat history retrieval, renaming, stats, clearing, notes, demo queries, and chat context analysis.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Flask's stream_with_context with a generator to implement server-sent JSON streaming for both chat answers and TTS audio output.

nodes.name: get_limiter
nodes.summary: Retrieves the Flask-Limiter extension instance from the current app context for rate limiting routes.

nodes.name: get_image_caption
nodes.summary: Encodes an image file as base64 and posts it to an external captioning service to obtain a descriptive caption.

nodes.name: trial_ask
nodes.summary: Rate-limited trial endpoint accepting an optional image and query, delegating answer generation to the query service for unauthenticated users.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Primary authenticated chat endpoint that accepts text and optional images, authenticates the session, and returns an answer via the query service.

nodes.name: ask_stream
nodes.summary: Authenticated streaming chat endpoint that uses guardrails, chat context, and a creative reasoning service to stream JSON-chunked answers back to the client.

nodes.name: ask_tts
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that answers a query via the query service and then streams the answer as synthesized speech audio using the TTS service.

nodes.name: synthesize
nodes.summary: Rate-limited, authenticated endpoint that converts arbitrary input text directly into streamed synthesized speech audio.

nodes.name: tts_health
nodes.summary: Authenticated health check endpoint that verifies connectivity to the text-to-speech backend service.

nodes.name: stt_transcribe
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that accepts an uploaded audio file and returns its transcription via the speech-to-text service.

nodes.name: stt_health
nodes.summary: Authenticated health check endpoint that verifies connectivity to the speech-to-text backend service.

nodes.name: toggle_note
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that toggles the saved-note flag on a specific chat message via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: list_notes
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that lists all messages a user has flagged as saved notes for a session.

nodes.name: get_chat_history
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that retrieves (and lazily creates) a chat's message history with pagination, generating default chat names as needed.

nodes.name: list_chats
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that lists all chat sessions belonging to a user via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: rename_chat
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that renames a specific chat session via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: get_chat_history_stats
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint returning aggregate statistics about a user's chat session history.

nodes.name: clear_chat_history
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that deletes a single chat session's history via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: clear_all_chats
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that deletes all chat sessions for a given user/session via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: demo
nodes.summary: Rate-limited demo endpoint that delegates query processing to the query service's demo query flow.

nodes.name: analyze_chat_context
nodes.summary: Authenticated endpoint that analyzes whether a new query needs prior chat context, using session stats and a chat context detection service.

nodes.name: chat_models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the core data model classes for the chat subsystem: query/role enums, chat messages, chat sessions, and chat context, including serialization to and from dictionaries.

nodes.name: QueryType
nodes.summary: Enumeration of supported chat query categories used to classify and route messages.

nodes.name: MessageRole
nodes.summary: Enumeration of chat message roles (e.g., user/assistant/system) used throughout the chat history model.

nodes.name: ChatMessage
nodes.summary: Represents a single chat message with metadata such as role, content, query type, token count, and optional image caption; supports dict serialization for persistence.

nodes.name: ChatSession
nodes.summary: Represents a full chat session containing an ordered list of messages, with helpers to fetch recent messages, conversation pairs, and serialize/deserialize the session.

nodes.name: ChatContext
nodes.summary: Represents derived context (relevant prior messages, summary, confidence score) used to enrich answer generation with conversational history.

nodes.name: document_service.py
nodes.summary: Core orchestration service that classifies uploaded files, routes them to document/data/URL processing pipelines, and manages document container lifecycle (create, rename, delete, fetch sessions) for the icarKno platform.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of background threading (threading.Thread) to run summarization and table-info extraction asynchronously after the main upload response is returned.

nodes.name: classify_files
nodes.summary: Splits an uploaded file list into document files, tabular/data files, and unsupported files based on file extension.

nodes.name: process_document_files
nodes.summary: Extracts text from document files, stores vectors for search, and kicks off background abstractive summarization for a user session.

nodes.name: process_data_files
nodes.summary: Creates or extends a SQL database from uploaded tabular files and triggers background table-info storage.

nodes.name: process_urls
nodes.summary: Delegates URL ingestion to the URL content service, stores resulting documents as vectors, and triggers background summarization.

nodes.name: DocumentService
nodes.summary: Main facade class coordinating file/URL upload processing, container (session) deletion, renaming, timestamp updates, and session listing for a user.

nodes.name: get_document_service
nodes.summary: Factory function returning a DocumentService instance.

nodes.name: file_storage_service.py
nodes.summary: Manages on-disk storage of uploaded files per user session, including saving, locating, listing, and deleting files and session directories.

nodes.name: FileStorageService
nodes.summary: Encapsulates filesystem operations for uploaded documents: filename sanitization, per-session directories, saving single/multiple files, existence checks, listing, and deletion.

nodes.name: get_file_storage_service
nodes.summary: Factory function returning a FileStorageService instance.

nodes.name: url_content_service.py
nodes.summary: Fetches and extracts content from arbitrary web URLs and YouTube videos (via transcript API or metadata scraping), converting results into LangChain Document objects for downstream ingestion.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a layered scraping strategy: static requests/BeautifulSoup first, falling back to a Selenium headless Chrome driver for JS-rendered pages.

nodes.name: UrlContentService
nodes.summary: Processes a list of URLs, normalizing them, distinguishing YouTube from generic web pages, and extracting clean text content for each via static or dynamic (Selenium) scraping.

nodes.name: get_url_content_service
nodes.summary: Factory function returning a UrlContentService instance.

nodes.name: delete_session.py
nodes.summary: Handles complete teardown of a user session: removing uploaded files from disk, deleting the associated Elasticsearch index, and clearing chat history.
nodes.languageNotes: Retains legacy/backward-compatible wrapper functions (delete_session_legacy, delete_session_original) that delegate to the current implementation.

nodes.name: delete_directory
nodes.summary: Removes a directory and its contents from disk if it exists.

nodes.name: delete_elastic_index
nodes.summary: Deletes an Elasticsearch index by name if it exists, using the shared ElasticClient.

nodes.name: delete_chat_history
nodes.summary: Deletes chat history records for a given user session via the chat history manager.

nodes.name: delete_session
nodes.summary: Orchestrates full session deletion by removing session files, the Elasticsearch index, and chat history, aggregating partial failures into a result report.

nodes.name: delete_session_legacy
nodes.summary: Backward-compatible wrapper that calls delete_session and returns a simplified boolean-style result.

nodes.name: delete_session_original
nodes.summary: Deprecated alias that forwards to delete_session_legacy for backward compatibility.

nodes.name: upload.py
nodes.summary: Processes extracted document text into hierarchical markdown-aware chunks, persists raw/chunked text to disk, and stores documents into Elasticsearch for hybrid search.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses LangChain's MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter combined with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter to produce hierarchy-aware chunks tagged with section breadcrumbs.

nodes.name: process_file_content
nodes.summary: Persists raw extracted text and hierarchical chunk JSON for a processed file into the user's session folder on disk.

nodes.name: get_hierarchical_chunks
nodes.summary: Splits document pages into hierarchy-aware chunks using markdown header and recursive character splitters, tagging each chunk with its section path and page number.

nodes.name: process_single_file
nodes.summary: Processes a single extracted document's text end-to-end: cleans filename, persists content, generates chunks, and stores them into Elasticsearch via ElasticDocumentManager.

nodes.name: store_vector
nodes.summary: Iterates over a batch of raw extracted texts, processes and stores each as vectors/search documents, and aggregates per-file results including chunk/page counts.

nodes.name: extractText.py
nodes.summary: Multi-format text extraction utility supporting TXT, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX files, with text cleaning, table-to-markdown conversion, and page/table metadata tracking; also runnable as a standalone CLI.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses asyncio.run_in_executor to offload CPU-bound parsing (fitz/PyMuPDF, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl) to a thread pool, and exposes a CLI via argparse/main() for standalone extraction testing.

nodes.name: _table_rows_to_markdown
nodes.summary: Converts a list of table row data into a GitHub-flavored markdown table string.

nodes.name: clean_filename
nodes.summary: Strips session/timestamp prefixes from an uploaded filename to recover the original display name.

nodes.name: clean_text
nodes.summary: Normalizes extracted text by fixing unicode artifacts, removing control characters, and collapsing redundant whitespace/punctuation patterns.

nodes.name: detect_file_type
nodes.summary: Determines a file's MIME type/category from its path and filename extension for extraction dispatch.

nodes.name: extract_txt
nodes.summary: Asynchronously reads and cleans plain text file content into a LangChain Document.

nodes.name: extract_pdf
nodes.summary: Extracts per-page text and detected tables (converted to markdown) from a PDF using PyMuPDF, producing a Document per page/table with cleaned text.

nodes.name: extract_docx
nodes.summary: Extracts paragraph text and tables from a Word document, mapping content to approximate page numbers and converting tables to markdown.

nodes.name: extract_pptx
nodes.summary: Extracts slide titles, text shapes, and tables from a PowerPoint presentation, one Document per slide/table.

nodes.name: extract_xlsx
nodes.summary: Extracts sheet data from an Excel workbook into pipe-delimited table text, producing a Document per sheet.

nodes.name: extract_content_from_file
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the appropriate format-specific extractor based on detected file type and aggregates extraction metadata (page count, char count).

nodes.name: get_text_from_files
nodes.summary: Synchronous entry point that runs an internal async extraction routine over multiple files concurrently and returns combined documents plus per-file metadata.

nodes.name: extract_from_path
nodes.summary: Convenience async helper that extracts content directly from a file path for CLI/testing use.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses command-line arguments and runs extraction against a given file path, printing results or writing output to disk.

nodes.name: accounts.py
nodes.summary: Flask Blueprint exposing account management API routes for updating payment plans, checking payment/subscription status, and user login authentication.

nodes.name: update_payment
nodes.summary: POST route handler that updates a user's payment plan by delegating to the account service and returning a JSON response.

nodes.name: check_payment_status
nodes.summary: POST route handler that retrieves a user's current payment/subscription status via the account service.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: POST route handler that authenticates a user via email/password and returns a session token through the account service.

nodes.name: account_service.py
nodes.summary: Service layer encapsulating account business logic for payment plan upgrades, payment status lookups, and user login, delegating persistence to the database controller.

nodes.name: AccountService
nodes.summary: Service class providing methods to upgrade a user's payment plan, fetch payment status, and validate login credentials, wrapping database controller calls with logging and error handling.

nodes.name: get_account_service
nodes.summary: Factory function that constructs and returns an AccountService instance, used as the singleton accessor by API routes.

nodes.name: query_service.py
nodes.summary: Core query orchestration service that processes trial, authenticated, and demo user queries, applying input guardrails, rate limits, language translation, and delegating to the query agent for answer generation.

nodes.name: QueryService
nodes.summary: Main service class coordinating the full query lifecycle: trial limit checks, input guardrail validation, query parameter extraction with translation, and dispatching to the query agent for trial, authenticated, and demo flows.

nodes.name: get_query_service
nodes.summary: Factory function that constructs and returns a QueryService instance for use by API route handlers.

nodes.name: database.py
nodes.summary: Database controller providing direct MongoDB-backed functions for trial fingerprint tracking, user rate limiting, account upgrades, password hashing/authentication, JWT session creation, and chat session management (rename, timestamp updates, deletion, listing).

nodes.name: check_trial_status
nodes.summary: Looks up or creates a trial fingerprint record in the database to track anonymous trial usage.

nodes.name: create_fingerprint_entry
nodes.summary: Creates or updates a fingerprint collection entry used to track trial usage counts for anonymous users.

nodes.name: is_trial_limit_over
nodes.summary: Checks whether an anonymous trial user (identified by fingerprint) has exceeded their allotted query limit, incrementing usage count on each call.

nodes.name: is_user_limit_over
nodes.summary: Checks whether an authenticated user has exceeded their daily/session query quota, updating usage counters in the database.

nodes.name: upgrade_account
nodes.summary: Upgrades a user's account by extending their subscription plan expiry date in the database.

nodes.name: get_account_status
nodes.summary: Fetches a user's account record and computes payment/subscription status based on plan expiry date versus current date.

nodes.name: sha512
nodes.summary: Computes an HMAC-SHA512 hash of a password using a provided salt.

nodes.name: salt_hash_password
nodes.summary: Hashes a user password with a configured secret salt for secure storage and comparison.

nodes.name: validate_user
nodes.summary: Validates a user's email and password against stored credentials and issues a JWT token on successful authentication.

nodes.name: create_session
nodes.summary: Creates a new chat session for a user in the database, recording associated files and timestamps.

nodes.name: add_files_to_session
nodes.summary: Appends additional uploaded file names to an existing chat session's document record.

nodes.name: rename_session
nodes.summary: Renames an existing chat session identified by session ID in the database.

nodes.name: update_session_timestamp
nodes.summary: Updates the last-active timestamp of a user's chat session to the current time.

nodes.name: delete_session_from_db
nodes.summary: Deletes a chat session record for a user from the database.

nodes.name: get_user_sessions
nodes.summary: Retrieves and sorts all chat sessions belonging to a given user from the database.

nodes.name: guardrails.py
nodes.summary: Input security pipeline implementing sanitization, malicious pattern detection (e.g. prompt injection), and LLM-based classification, composed into a configurable SecurityPipeline used to validate user queries before processing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a strategy/pipeline pattern with composable handler functions (sanitizer, pattern checker, LLM classifier) wired together via factory functions, allowing custom guardrail pipelines to be assembled.

nodes.name: InputSanitizer
nodes.summary: Sanitizes raw input text by escaping configured characters and stripping text matching a removal regex pattern.

nodes.name: MaliciousPatternChecker
nodes.summary: Checks input text against a set of compiled regex patterns to detect malicious content such as injection attempts, returning matching pattern details.

nodes.name: LLMClassifier
nodes.summary: Uses a fast LLM to classify whether input text is safe or malicious based on a configurable validation prompt.

nodes.name: SecurityPipeline
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full input guardrail pipeline by running custom handlers, sanitization, pattern checking, and LLM classification in sequence and aggregating the results.

nodes.name: create_sanitizer
nodes.summary: Factory function that builds an InputSanitizer configured with escape character mappings and a removal regex pattern.

nodes.name: create_pattern_checker
nodes.summary: Factory function that builds a MaliciousPatternChecker configured with a list of detection patterns and case sensitivity option.

nodes.name: create_llm_classifier
nodes.summary: Factory function that builds an LLMClassifier configured with a custom validation prompt.

nodes.name: input_guardrail_pipeline
nodes.summary: Builds and returns the default SecurityPipeline composed of a standard sanitizer, pattern checker, and LLM classifier, used as the main entry point for input validation.

nodes.name: create_custom_pipeline
nodes.summary: Builds a customized SecurityPipeline allowing callers to override the sanitizer, pattern checker, LLM classifier, and additional custom handlers.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Flask application's configuration system: a BaseConfig with environment-driven settings (Elasticsearch, MongoDB, MySQL, JWT, rate limiting, Ollama, Vexyl STT/TTS, GPU server, document summary tuning) plus Development/Testing/Production subclasses and a ConfigFactory to select and validate the active config.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses os.getenv with defaults plus a static validate() method overridden per-environment (e.g., TestingConfig skips validation) — a simple config-factory pattern common in Flask apps.

nodes.name: BaseConfig
nodes.summary: Base configuration class holding shared settings for secret keys, Elasticsearch/MongoDB/MySQL connections, JWT, rate limiting, Ollama models, Vexyl TTS/STT URLs, GPU server parameters, and document summary tuning values, plus a validate() check for required environment variables.

nodes.name: DevelopmentConfig
nodes.summary: Development environment configuration that enables DEBUG mode, inheriting all other settings from BaseConfig.

nodes.name: TestingConfig
nodes.summary: Testing environment configuration that enables DEBUG/TESTING flags, points MONGO_URL at a local test database, and overrides validate() to skip required-variable checks.

nodes.name: ProductionConfig
nodes.summary: Production environment configuration enforcing a stronger SECRET_KEY requirement and stricter rate limiting defaults.

nodes.name: ConfigFactory
nodes.summary: Factory class that maps a config name string (development/testing/production/default) to the corresponding config class, running validate() except in testing mode.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: Provides a singleton ElasticClient wrapper that lazily initializes and exposes a shared Elasticsearch connection, with ping and index_exists helper methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the singleton pattern via __new__ to ensure a single shared Elasticsearch client instance across the application.

nodes.name: ElasticClient
nodes.summary: Singleton wrapper around the Elasticsearch Python client; initializes the connection from Config.ES_BASE_URL on first use and exposes ping() and index_exists() helpers.

nodes.name: document_manager.py
nodes.summary: Manages storing documents into Elasticsearch with embeddings, including Unicode/Hindi-aware preprocessing before indexing via ElasticsearchStore; update/delete operations are stubbed as TODOs.
nodes.languageNotes: Normalizes text with unicodedata.normalize('NFC', ...) to ensure consistent multilingual (Hindi) Unicode handling before embedding and indexing.

nodes.name: ElasticDocumentManager
nodes.summary: Coordinates document ingestion into an Elasticsearch index: preprocesses documents for Unicode normalization, ensures the index exists, embeds and stores documents via ElasticsearchStore, and refreshes the index. update_documents and delete_documents are unimplemented placeholders.

nodes.name: index_manager.py
nodes.summary: Manages Elasticsearch index lifecycle (create, delete, refresh, existence checks) using a custom mapping with dense_vector embeddings and Hindi/multilingual text analyzers.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines a custom Elasticsearch mapping with a hindi_analyzer and multilingual_analyzer, plus a dense_vector field (1024 dims) for hybrid keyword+vector search support.

nodes.name: ElasticIndexManager
nodes.summary: Manages Elasticsearch index lifecycle operations — creating indices with a multilingual/vector-aware mapping (with retry-based readiness checks), deleting, refreshing, and checking existence.

nodes.name: retriever.py
nodes.summary: Implements hybrid (keyword + vector) document retrieval over Elasticsearch using an EnsembleRetriever, with LLM-based query enrichment that rewrites queries using chat context, plus a helper to fetch all chunks belonging to a table for full-table retrieval.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines a custom ElasticsearchRetriever (keyword search with Hindi-aware fields) and an ElasticsearchStore vector retriever into a weighted EnsembleRetriever (0.4/0.6), and uses an LLM call to enrich/rewrite the query before keyword search.

nodes.name: ElasticRetriever
nodes.summary: Performs hybrid keyword+vector search against an Elasticsearch index by combining a custom keyword retriever and a vector store retriever into an EnsembleRetriever; enriches user queries via an LLM call (optionally using chat context) before keyword search, and supports fetching full table chunks beyond the top-k limit.

nodes.name: chat_context_service.py
nodes.summary: Detects whether a follow-up query needs prior conversation context (via regex patterns plus LLM fallback) and extracts the relevant slice of chat history to feed into downstream prompts.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines fast regex-based heuristics with an LLM-based fallback, merging both signals via a confidence-weighted combination step before extracting context using one of several specialized strategies (recent, reference, clarification, continuation, adaptive).

nodes.name: ChatContextService
nodes.summary: Core service that detects context-dependency in user queries and extracts the most relevant chat history segment using regex pattern matching combined with an LLM-based classifier.

nodes.name: get_chat_context_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton accessor that constructs and returns a ChatContextService instance.

nodes.name: query_agent_service.py
nodes.summary: Top-level orchestrator for the query pipeline: combines intent classification, chat context retrieval, document/data/hybrid context lookup, optional creative reasoning mode, and response generation into a single process_query entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as a facade composing five other services (intent, context provider, response generator, chat history, chat context, and an optional creative reasoning service) and dispatches to mode-specific handlers (document, data, hybrid, summary, general chat).

nodes.name: QueryAgentService
nodes.summary: Main query-processing facade that wires together intent classification, context retrieval, chat history, and response generation, exposing process_query as the primary API used by callers to answer user questions against documents and structured data.

nodes.name: get_query_agent_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton accessor that constructs and returns a QueryAgentService instance.

nodes.name: query_intent_service.py
nodes.summary: Classifies a user query's intent (general chat, summary request, data query, or document-context-needed) using an LLM-backed classifier so the query agent can route to the correct response strategy.

nodes.name: QueryIntent
nodes.summary: Simple data/enum-like class representing the possible query intent categories used throughout the routing logic.

nodes.name: QueryIntentService
nodes.summary: Classifies incoming queries into general-chat, summary, data, or document-context categories by chaining several LLM-backed boolean checks.

nodes.name: get_query_intent_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton accessor that constructs and returns a QueryIntentService instance.

nodes.name: response_generator_service.py
nodes.summary: Generates the final natural-language responses for every query mode (general chat, document, data, hybrid, document-aware chat) by building mode-specific prompts, invoking the LLM, parsing structured JSON-like output, and translating results to the user's requested language.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of regex-based structured-response extraction and JSON parsing fallbacks to robustly handle LLM output that may not strictly follow the requested format, plus an integration point with the translation utility for multi-language output.

nodes.name: ResponseGeneratorService
nodes.summary: Builds prompts and generates structured, translated responses for general chat, document, data, hybrid, and document-aware chat query modes, parsing and validating the LLM's structured output before returning it to callers.

nodes.name: get_response_generator_service
nodes.summary: Factory/singleton accessor that constructs and returns a ResponseGeneratorService instance.

nodes.name: translation.py
nodes.summary: Translation utility that delegates to a remote IndicTrans2 inference server, providing translate_to_indic and translate_to_english helpers for converting text between English and 23 Indic languages using FLORES-200 language codes.
nodes.languageNotes: Configuration (server URL, API key, timeout) is read once at import time from environment variables; sentence splitting is used to keep translation requests within manageable chunk sizes for the remote service.

nodes.name: _headers
nodes.summary: Builds the HTTP Authorization header dict for requests to the translation server, using the API key if configured.

nodes.name: translate_to_indic
nodes.summary: Translates English text into a target Indic language by calling the remote IndicTrans2 inference server, validating the language against the FLORES-200 mapping before making the request.

nodes.name: translate_to_english
nodes.summary: Translates text from a source Indic language (identified by numeric language ID) into English via the remote translation server.

nodes.name: _split_into_sentences
nodes.summary: Splits a block of text into individual sentences using regex, used to chunk text before sending to the translation server.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what icarKno is: an AI-powered document intelligence platform that lets users upload PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, CSV/XLSX and other formats, then query them with natural language using hybrid keyword+vector search, multi-step AI reasoning, and multi-language (23+ languages) support. The README also documents the architecture, project structure, and Docker-based deployment, giving you the roadmap this tour will walk through in code.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: run.py is the literal starting point of the running system: it imports the Flask application factory and launches the dev server bound to 0.0.0.0:5001 in production mode. It has the lowest fan-in in the whole graph (nothing else depends on it) yet it is where execution begins, which is the classic signature of an entry point versus a library module.

tour.title: The Application Factory
tour.description: app/__init__.py is the module run.py actually calls into. It builds and configures the Flask app: setting up logging, loading environment-specific configuration via ConfigFactory, enabling CORS, initializing extensions, registering every API blueprint, and defining global JSON error handlers. This factory pattern is what wires together everything else you'll see in this tour -- the API layer, the config system, and the rate-limiting extensions.
tour.languageLesson: The 'application factory' pattern (create_app()) lets Flask apps be instantiated multiple times with different configs -- essential for testing and for running dev/staging/production from the same codebase without global state leaking between instances.

tour.title: Centralized Configuration
tour.description: app/config.py is the second-most depended-upon file in the codebase (11 incoming references), meaning nearly every service and controller reads its settings. It defines a BaseConfig with environment-driven settings for Elasticsearch, MongoDB, MySQL, JWT, rate limiting, the GPU inference server, and Vexyl STT/TTS, plus Development/Testing/Production subclasses selected through a ConfigFactory. Pair this with .env.example, which documents every environment variable -- API keys, database credentials, and speech service settings -- that BaseConfig expects to find.
tour.languageLesson: Python's class-inheritance config pattern (BaseConfig -> DevelopmentConfig/ProductionConfig) keeps shared defaults in one place while letting each environment override only what differs, avoiding scattered if-environment-equals checks throughout the codebase.

tour.title: Document Upload and Container Management
tour.description: app/api/documents.py is the Flask blueprint that implements the README's first feature: getting documents into the system. It exposes routes for free-trial uploads, authenticated file/URL uploads, file retrieval, and container (session) renaming/listing/deletion. Every route delegates real work to document_service.py, keeping the blueprint itself thin -- a pattern you'll see repeated across the API layer.

tour.title: Document Processing Pipeline
tour.description: document_service.py has the highest fan-out in the entire codebase (8 outgoing dependencies), making it the busiest orchestrator: it classifies uploaded files by type, routes them to document, data, or URL processing pipelines, and manages the lifecycle of each user's document container. file_storage_service.py handles the actual on-disk persistence of those files per session, and url_content_service.py extracts content from arbitrary web pages and YouTube videos so they can be ingested the same way as uploaded files.

tour.title: Text Extraction and Chunking
tour.description: Once document_service.py knows what kind of file it has, utils/extractText.py does the heavy lifting: pulling clean text out of PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and TXT files, converting tables to markdown, and tracking page/table metadata. controllers/upload.py then takes that raw text and produces hierarchical, markdown-aware chunks -- the unit of retrieval that Elasticsearch will later search over. This is the 'intelligent chunking' the README promises for optimal retrieval.

tour.title: Elasticsearch: Index and Storage
tour.description: With chunks in hand, three elastic/ modules persist them for search. elastic/client.py is a singleton wrapper around the shared Elasticsearch connection; elastic/index_manager.py creates and manages the index itself using a custom mapping with dense_vector embeddings plus Hindi/multilingual text analyzers; and elastic/document_manager.py stores the chunked documents with embeddings, applying Unicode/Hindi-aware preprocessing before indexing. Together these three implement the storage half of the README's 'hybrid search' feature.

tour.title: Hybrid Retrieval
tour.description: elastic/retriever.py is the read-side counterpart to Step 8's write-side storage: it implements hybrid keyword+vector retrieval using an EnsembleRetriever, with LLM-based query enrichment that rewrites queries using chat context before searching, plus a helper for fetching every chunk belonging to a specific table. This is what the README calls 'Hybrid Search: Combines keyword and vector search for best results.'

tour.title: The LLM Service Hub
tour.description: app/services/llm_service.py has by far the highest fan-in in the codebase (13 incoming dependencies) -- nearly every reasoning, search, and synthesis service you'll meet next calls into it. It defines a custom LangChain-compatible chat model that talks to a self-hosted GPU inference server, and exposes factory functions for differently-tuned LLM instances (fast, standard, comprehensive, creative, code, streaming). This hub-and-spoke shape is exactly what you'd expect from a shared infrastructure dependency: everything needs an LLM, so everything imports this one module.
tour.languageLesson: Factory functions like get_fast_llm()/get_creative_llm() that all funnel through a private _make_llm() helper are a common way to expose multiple pre-configured variants of an expensive object without duplicating construction logic.

tour.title: Multi-Step Reasoning Pipeline
tour.description: This cluster of services implements the README's 'Creative Reasoning: Advanced multi-step analysis for complex queries.' reasoning_strategy_service.py decomposes a query into a structured multi-step search strategy; search_execution_service.py executes that strategy by building a dependency-ordered plan and running document/SQL/summary/hybrid searches through context_provider_service.py (which centralizes retrieval across Elasticsearch, the SQL database, and the summarizer); adaptive_search_service.py iteratively refines queries across rounds using result_evaluation_service.py's LLM-based sufficiency judgments; and result_synthesis_service.py formats everything with citations into a final structured, streamable answer. creative_reasoning_service.py ties all of this together as the orchestrator for open-ended queries.

tour.title: Structured Data: SQL and Summarization
tour.description: Not every query is about unstructured text. controllers/sql_db.py manages per-session SQLite databases created from uploaded CSV/Excel files, converting natural-language questions into SQL via an LLM chain and executing them safely -- this is the README's 'SQL Generation: Automatic conversion of questions to database queries' feature. controllers/doc_summary.py complements it with extractive (BERT-based) and LLM-driven abstractive summarization across a session's uploaded files. Both are part of the older controllers/ layer that predates the app/api blueprint structure, but context_provider_service.py from Step 11 calls directly into them, showing how the new service layer wraps rather than replaces this legacy code.

tour.title: The Query Pipeline and Chat API
tour.description: app/api/queries.py is the second-busiest API file (6 outgoing dependencies) and the largest blueprint in the project: it powers trial/authenticated Q&A (sync and streaming), image captioning, chat history, notes, and demo queries. Every request flows through query_agent_service.py, the top-level orchestrator that combines intent classification (query_intent_service.py), chat context retrieval, and the reasoning pipeline from Steps 10-11 into a single process_query call, while response_generator_service.py builds the final mode-specific prompt and translates the answer into the user's requested language. chat_models.py defines the ChatMessage/ChatSession/ChatContext data classes that flow through this entire pipeline, and chat_history_manager.py persists them to MongoDB.

tour.title: Security, Translation, and Voice
tour.description: Three utility-layer services support every query above. utils/guardrails.py is a SecurityPipeline that sanitizes input and detects prompt-injection attempts before a query is ever processed -- query_service.py applies these guardrails up front. utils/translation.py delegates to a remote IndicTrans2 server to translate between English and 23 Indic languages, implementing the README's multi-language support. app/services/stt_service.py and tts_service.py round out the README's voice features by connecting to an external Vexyl backend for speech-to-text and text-to-speech, both wired into app/api/queries.py's /stt and /tts routes from Step 13.

tour.title: Accounts, Auth, and API Reference
tour.description: Rounding out the platform, app/api/accounts.py and account_service.py implement subscription/payment plan management and login, backed by controllers/database.py's direct MongoDB functions for password hashing, JWT session creation, and rate limiting -- another example of the service layer delegating to the legacy controllers layer. To see how all of these pieces -- documents, queries, accounts, speech, and translation -- come together as a consumable REST surface, consult api-documentation.md, which documents every endpoint this tour has touched, including the WhatsApp webhook integration mentioned in the README.
